children: Condé Nast Chief Executive Roger Lynch is stepping down after more than seven years to become CEO of toy company Mattel.

Mike Perlis, the former CEO of Forbes and Ziff-Davis Publishing, as well as Condé Nast's lead independent board member, will become Condé Nast's interim CEO while the board searches for a new executive, the company said Wednesday.

Mattel, the maker of Barbie dolls and Hot Wheels cars, has spent years trying to transform into a toy and entertainment company. During Lynch's time at the helm, Condé Nast, which owns Vogue, the New Yorker and Vanity Fair, faced challenges.

Artificial intelligence is transforming the way people seek and consume information, hurting web traffic to many publishers, and social-media platforms such as TikTok have diverted audiences' attention and diluted the influence of magazines that once set the cultural agenda.
Advertising, once the bedrock of the magazine business, has faced significant pressure across the industry.
"We navigated a pandemic, enormous disruption across our industry, and a media landscape that seemed to change beneath our feet every year," Lynch said in a note to staff announcing his departure.

He described in the memo the company's efforts to unify its global businesses and strengthen its consumer and events businesses. The company launched a new Middle East office in Dubai, invested in products like e-commerce platform Vette and gave priority to events like Vogue World, he wrote.
Lynch, a board member at Mattel since 2018, will remain on the Condé Nast board.
